title: Senior Employer Branding Specialist
description:
Brief info about Vinted 

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life – or even a third.
The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

Information about the position 

Our team’s mission is to align Vinted’s values, business goals, and Employer Value Proposition with our people’s real work experience. We translate Vinted’s truth into an inspiring story that attracts the right people, helps them grow, and instils them with pride.

You’ll take an active role in Employer Branding at Vinted, with a particular focus on attracting engineering and data science talent. You’ll be based in Amsterdam, where our data science team is growing, but your work will reach candidates around the world.

Vinted has become an ecosystem with vertically integrated shipping and payments. This requires us to adapt our EVP to three very distinct brands and even more diversified hiring needs. Your job is to turn that into creative campaigns and stories that make specific audiences want to work here.

Our next big focus is storytelling. Bringing the skills and challenges our teams face to life! What is a day in the life of a cybersecurity analyst? How does an anti-money laundering expert keep members’ wallets safe? What does it take to build the data science behind a marketplace used by millions? And what stories does each of our locations need?

Partnering with Talent Acquisition, engineering and data science leaders, People, Marketing, PR, Internal Comms, and Brand & Design, you’ll make sure those stories are told and that our presence is strong where we hire.

In this position, you’ll 

  • Be the guardian of Vinted’s employer brand, ensuring consistency and visibility across all platforms, like LinkedIn and Instagram
  • Strong brand-building skills, with a clear vision of global vs local branding differentiation
  • Use your sound understanding of branding and our editorial guidelines to write clear and engaging copy for things such as blogs, advertising campaigns, employer branding assets, email campaigns, event materials, online company profiles, as well as our careers pages.
  • Create bespoke or support partnership events such as meetups, webinars, and networking events
  • Plan and run recruitment advertising, such as targeted LinkedIn campaigns and sponsorships with third-party publications and organisations, aimed at technical audiences.
  • Define where our global employer brand ends and local adaptation begins, so each location can tell its story while staying consistent with Vinted’s.
  • Shape our content calendar around hiring needs and our location strategy.
  • Track what works, using results to sharpen the next activation, and share learnings with the wider Employer Branding team.

About you 

  • Passionate about all things Employer Branding!
  • You love storytelling: finding stories and having a keen eye for telling them in ways that stand out. You can show campaigns or activations you conceived and delivered.
  • Background in building and nurturing online and offline communities, and delivering innovative events and social media campaigns.
  • A clear view of global vs local branding, and experience working across markets.
  • Adept at identifying new talent attraction channels, especially for engineering and data science audiences.
  • Comfortable using data to set goals and judge what worked.
  • Ability to juggle multiple projects with strong stakeholder management, and to work confidently with engineering and data science leaders.
  • Excited by change, a fast pace, and learning new ways of doing things.
  • Excellent knowledge of social media and digital channels, including LinkedIn, Glassdoor, Indeed, and Meta.
  • Excellent written and verbal English communication skills (English is Vinted’s official working language).

Work perks 

  • The opportunity to benefit from our share options programme
  • 25 days of paid annual leave
  • Newest MacBook models
  • Digital mental and emotional health support and Employee Assistant Program (EAP)
  • Frequent team-building events
  • Home office support: we provide IT workstation equipment and a personal budget of up to €540 for home workplace furniture
  • Lunch benefit per working day
  • Company bike leasing scheme
  • Monthly budget for a flexible benefits platform
  • Work from Home allowance
  • A personal monthly budget for shopping on Vinted
  • Collective Defined Contribution Pension plan
  • NS Business Card for your commute to the office by public transport
  • A dog-friendly office

Working at Vinted 

Workation policy

Better balance holidays with workdays by working remotely! Up to 90 days per year in the EU, of these, 21 days can be spent globally. For non-EU citizens, it's 21 days worldwide. This can be combined with time off for vacation or personal time.

Individual learning budget

Each year, you’ll be given a learning budget (starting at €3,000), and a total of up to 10 working days over a 2-year period to support your personal and professional development.

Hybrid work

Our hybrid model, with 2 recommended office days a week, gives you and your team the flexibility to decide if and when you want to work from home, and when to catch up in person.

Equal opportunity

We welcome applications from everybody, regardless of your background, identity, or life experiences. Job openings come with guides, not checklists. If you’re excited about a role, but don’t identify with every point in the ‘About you’ section, apply anyway – you might still be the perfect match!

The annual gross salary range for this position excluding 8% holiday pay is:
€59.800—€81.000 EUR

title: AI Platform Engineer
description: About Supabase Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth. About the Role We are hiring a AI Platform Engineer to build the execution layer for Supabase's internal AI systems. Supabase is building an AI-native internal operating system: a common way of working across the company where AI carries a meaningful share of the operational load rather than sitting alongside it as an assistant. We are standing up a new central team to build those systems, enable the teams, and embed AI operations throughout the organization. You are the engineer on that team. The execution layer is yours. You will build the platform that actually runs agents: an event-triggered queue, a headless model-agnostic runtime, durable state so work survives a restart, a human review gate, atomic rollback, and full logging of every prompt, tool call and decision so any run can be reconstructed. You will build the evaluation layer that makes any of it trustworthy, because an agent that cannot be measured cannot be trusted with anything beyond reading. And you will build the agents themselves, across everything from executive reporting down to a layer of agents that watch the platform and improve it. This is a governance-heavy environment by design, and that is the interesting part of the problem. Agents are risk-tiered from read-only internal data through to external-facing output, with review depth, evaluation requirements and human approval scaling by tier. Some capabilities are permanently off limits: an agent may read and report, it may carry a human-authored update into a system of record once a human consents, and it may initiate contact within a strict budget, but it may never autonomously write a commitment (an owner, a due date, a status) into a shared work system. Your job is to make that structurally impossible rather than merely forbidden. You will be the only engineer on this platform. You will close open architecture decisions yourself, own the infrastructure end to end, and instrument the system so it reports its own return. What You'll Be Responsible For In this role, you'll: Ship the agent platform to production. An event-triggered queue, a headless model-agnostic runtime (choosing the runtime is an open decision you will close), durable state that survives a failed run, a human review gate, atomic rollback, and complete run logging in the warehouse. Own the evaluation layer, and switch on the gate that depends on it. Golden suites with behavioral assertions rather than intuition, judge criteria with a written rubric, safety cases that must pass on every run, and a CI gate that blocks a regression from merging. This is the precondition for every agent that does anything beyond read internal data. Build and register the agent portfolio. Reporting, drafting, linting, triage and question-answering agents across the executive, team-lead and individual-contributor layers, plus a meta layer that observes the platform and improves it. Enforce governance in code. Risk tiers the pipeline actually enforces, least-privilege credentials per agent, tool-permission gates, a decision audit log, and autonomy classes where the dangerous class has no code path rather than a warning label. Nothing runs without a registered owner, tier, tool grant and human gate. Design how the system contacts people. A hard interruption budget per person, message bundling instead of a stream of pings, and a structure that gives something useful before it asks for anything. Adoption depends on this more than on any other single design choice. Own the platform tooling. The compiler and validator, inventory integrity, and the paths that distribute context and capabilities into the repositories and chat surfaces where work happens. Compute the operating measures from production data. A pipeline from raw system activity through to a computed maturity grade per team, defensible enough that a team can dispute the result and be answered with the query rather than an opinion. Instrument the platform's own return. A ledger that logs the work each agent absorbs and computes the monthly figure, so the value of the system is a measurement rather than a claim. How You'll Think Recursive Thinking You build the generator, not the artifact. When you need thirty agents, you do not write thirty agents; you build the inventory, the compiler and the distribution path that makes the thirty-first cost an afternoon, then a meta layer whose job is to watch the platform, find its drift and file the fix. The evaluation layer is the same move applied to trust. You are not checking whether one agent is correct today. You are building the machine that decides whether every future agent is allowed to ship, which means the suite has to be right in a way the agent does not, and the thing that grades has to be graded too. Inversion Thinking You start from the failure and work backward to the design. The rule is that an agent may never autonomously write a commitment into a shared work system. The weak implementation is an instruction in a prompt. The strong one is that the credential in the agent's tool grant physically cannot set an owner, a due date or a status, so no amount of clever input, prompt injection or model error produces the forbidden write. You reach for the second one first. Same for evaluation. Before writing a suite you enumerate how the agent can be wrong: an update that invents progress that did not happen, one that quotes a private channel into a public digest, one that is accurate and reads as an accusation, one that credits the wrong person. Then the suite is that list, each case caught before the agent ships rather than after it embarrasses someone. AI-Native Execution You use agentic tools on real work, in files and repositories, with the same rigor you apply to anything else you ship. You have a setup of your own and can describe it mechanically: what triggers it, what it is allowed to touch, where the human approves, what it logs, and how you found out the one time it went wrong. That experience is this job, generalized. You are building for async engineers across 40+ countries who will judge the platform by whether it saves them an hour or costs them one, so you are your own first user and your own harshest reviewer. You Might Be a Good Fit If You Must Have Have shipped production LLM agent systems that other people depended on. Not demos, not internal showcases. Systems with operational history, real users and at least one incident you can talk through. Prompt engineering on its own does not clear this bar. Design evaluations, not spot checks. You build golden sets, write behavioral assertions, define judge rubrics, set pass thresholds and gate CI on the result. You can explain why "we reviewed a bunch of outputs and they looked good" is not evaluation. Have done deep API work against the systems work actually lives in , and have authored MCP servers. You know the specific failure modes of those APIs, not just that they exist. Own infrastructure end to end in Python on GCP, with a cloud warehouse and infrastructure as code. You provision, deploy, monitor and roll back your own systems, and you close architecture decisions rather than routing them onward. Have taste about how software contacts humans. You treat every notification as spending a limited amount of trust. Strong Signal Public work in this space. An open-source agent framework, an MCP server, an evaluation harness, or writing on agent reliability that other practitioners cite. LLM observability and cost instrumentation. Tracing agent runs, attributing spend per run, and building the queries that turn raw logs into a report someone acts on. You have built an internal platform that non-engineers adopted voluntarily , and can describe what you changed after watching them use it. What Success Looks Like The platform is boring. Agents run on a schedule and on events, state survives restarts, failed runs roll back cleanly, and every run can be reconstructed from its log. Nothing ships unevaluated. Every registered agent has a real suite with safety cases, the gate blocks regressions, and when someone challenges an output the answer is a test case rather than an argument. The dangerous action is impossible, not discouraged. An audit of any agent's credentials shows it cannot perform the writes it is not allowed to perform, and the audit log makes every consequential decision traceable. Teams pull the platform instead of being pushed. Agents get adopted because the reports are useful and the contact is rare and well-timed, and each team ends up with at least one workflow that runs automatically. The platform reports its own value. The work absorbed is measured and published, so the case for expanding it is made with data rather than enthusiasm. What We Offer Fully Remote We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world. ESOP Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together. Tech Allowance Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work. Health Benefits Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us. Annual Off-Sites Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year. Flexible Work We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when. Professional Development Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth. About the Team Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love. ~400 team members 60+ countries 20+ languages spoken Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F) 540,000+ community members We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

  • Public work in this space. An open-source agent framework, an MCP server, an evaluation harness, or writing on agent reliability that other practitioners cite.

  • LLM observability and cost instrumentation. Tracing agent runs, attributing spend per run, and building the queries that turn raw logs into a report someone acts on.

  • You have built an internal platform that non-engineers adopted voluntarily, and can describe what you changed after watching them use it.

What Success Looks Like

  • The platform is boring. Agents run on a schedule and on events, state survives restarts, failed runs roll back cleanly, and every run can be reconstructed from its log.

  • Nothing ships unevaluated. Every registered agent has a real suite with safety cases, the gate blocks regressions, and when someone challenges an output the answer is a test case rather than an argument.

  • The dangerous action is impossible, not discouraged. An audit of any agent's credentials shows it cannot perform the writes it is not allowed to perform, and the audit log makes every consequential decision traceable.

  • Teams pull the platform instead of being pushed. Agents get adopted because the reports are useful and the contact is rare and well-timed, and each team ends up with at least one workflow that runs automatically.

  • The platform reports its own value. The work absorbed is measured and published, so the case for expanding it is made with data rather than enthusiasm.

What We Offer

  • Fully Remote

    We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

  • ESOP

    Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

  • Tech Allowance

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

  • Health Benefits

    Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

  • Annual Off-Sites

    Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

  • Flexible Work

    We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

  • Professional Development

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

  • ~400 team members

  • 60+ countries

  • 20+ languages spoken

  • Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

  • 540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

Its modular, AI-powered infrastructure enables hoteliers to customise their tech stack, automate routine work, and deliver seamless, personalised guest experiences, powered by best-in-class apps and autonomous AI agents that adapt to every stay.

Why this role

You are the technical voice in front of strategic customers, at a moment when hospitality is being rebuilt around AI. We are launching our own AI agent platform, and we need architects who can show operators what comes next.

  • High freedom. You decide how to solve a problem, which tools to use and what to prototype.
  • Fast iteration. We test ideas within days, try new technology early and share what works.

Your mission

Win and grow strategic accounts with technical credibility, and turn what you learn in the field into input for the product. You look at a customer's current architecture and show how an Apaleo-centred setup delivers their goals. You also help them put AI agents to work, deciding what should be an agent, what it costs and how to set it up. Sales and Account Management own the relationship and the commercial terms. You own the technical answer.

What you will do

  • Technical discovery and solution scoping. Lead discovery where a standard demo is not enough. Write clear scopes covering what Apaleo delivers natively, what needs a short-term solution and what is out of scope.
  • Proofs of concept. Build fast, working proofs of concept (quick demos that show technical fit). Agree scope in writing first, and build in a safe test environment, never with live guest data.
  • Agents and automations. Design and build agents and automations for customer use cases, using n8n or Make today and Apaleo's own AI agent platform as it launches. Write code where agents need deterministic steps.
  • Hands-on delivery and short-term solutions. Work alongside the customer, building only where it unblocks a named deal, removes an adoption risk or fills a product gap. Agree an exit plan (an end date, a replacement and a named owner) before you start.
  • Post-sale health checks and expansions. Diagnose gaps against the go-live specification, run proactive checks (for example 90 days after go-live) and scope integrations for expanding customers.
  • Reusable assets. Turn every engagement into a reference architecture, pattern or template that the next twenty customers can use.
  • Thought leadership. Join prospect and customer conversations on how AI will change hospitality over the next two to three years.
  • Product feedback. Test new technology on real customer problems. Share prototypes and field evidence with Product, ending every experiment with a clear decision: adopt, hand over or drop.

How you work

  • You decide the approach, the stack and the order of work.
  • You protect three guardrails: written scope before a proof of concept, an exit plan before a custom build and no commercial promises.
  • You go from idea to prototype in days and show it early.
  • You think in systems and build for reuse, not one-off projects.
  • You share findings openly with Sales, Account Management and Product.

Who you work with

Sales/BD and Account Management (they call you in at defined deal triggers), Customer Success, Product, Security, Partnerships, RevOps and Senior Leadership.

  • Multiple years in solution architecture, solution engineering or technical consulting in B2B SaaS, ideally with complex software such as ERP or enterprise platforms
  • Strong API skills: REST, authentication, webhooks and events, and data-flow design
  • Hands-on workflow automation (n8n preferred) and practical experience building with LLM agents
  • A systems thinker with real AI curiosity, who uses AI tools day to day
  • Stakeholder management experience and credibility with executives and IT teams
  • Self-direction, an ownership mindset and the discipline to say no to scope that does not advance a deal
  • Curiosity that ends in working prototypes, not just opinions
  • Clear, structured documentation habits
  • Fluent English and French skills
  • Willingness to travel, including regularly to France and the UK

Strong plus

  • Hospitality or travel experience, including hotel operations and PMS concepts (reservations, folios, rate plans, night audit)
  • Experience with another cloud PMS, channel manager or payments integrations
  • Enterprise architecture experience on large, multi-site projects
  • Applied AI or ML background, or experience with MCP and agent platforms
  • SQL and BI fundamentals

How we measure success

  • Architecture engagements and blueprints delivered each quarter
  • Customer satisfaction with your contribution
  • Adoption of recommended apps, integrations and agents
  • Share of engagements served by an existing reusable pattern
  • Revenue impact e.g. deal unblocked, AI adoption, or churn averted

  • Days 1 to 30: Learn the platform and ways of working, shadow discovery and proof of concept work, and take over open customer projects.

  • Days 61 to 90: Deliver a proof of concept or short-term solution end to end with an exit plan, and share your first experiment with Product.

Our evolving career framework ensures you have increasing opportunities to learn new skills, advance your career, and make an impact.
  • Autonomy & Ownership: Great ideas can come from anywhere. We empower you to take responsibility, make decisions, and contribute directly in an environment built on trust, transparency, and collaboration.
  • Shape the Future of Hospitality Tech: Be part of a fast-growing scale-up transforming the hospitality industry. From day one, your work drives real impact and you’ll have the freedom to bring your ideas to life.
  • Competitive & Fair Compensation: We believe great work deserves great pay. Our salaries are competitive and guided by benchmarking data to ensure fairness across all roles and teams. We make sure to recognize and reward performance and contribution.

Perks & Lifestyle

  • Flexible & Remote Work Options: We focus on results, not clocking hours. You can work from home, the office or in a hybrid setup, with flexibility to adapt your schedule as long as it makes sense for your role, your team and our business.
  • Team Connection: Strong connections fuel collaboration. We celebrate and connect through regular team dinners, company meetups, Oktoberfest celebrations, Christmas parties, and other offsite events.

We embrace flexibility in where and how work gets done and also value meaningful in-person moments to connect and collaborate. You can expect a remote-first working model with periodic in-person gatherings at your closest office for team connection, planning, or other key moments.

  • Drive the design and architecture of complex, scalable systems that underpin our technology solutions. Capable of designing long-lasting systems to solve complex problems (including scalability, reliability, consistency and quality) often across an engineering pillar.
  • Conduct design reviews at both the engineering pillar level and across the broader engineering organization.
  • Leads generalisable improvements in operational maturity for his platform and promotes best practices with other engineers when it comes to operations.
  • Work closely with engineering managers, other principal and senior principal engineers to drive technology strategy and roadmap that aligns to the wider organisation vision.
  • Partners with Product Manager(s) and Engineering Manager(s) to establish clear technical delivery milestones for key initiatives and then helps to drive delivery within the agreed scope, quality and on time.
  • Build trusted leadership by being regarded as a go-to person across a wide number of technologies, practices, and tools used in an engineering pillar.
  • Communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders to ensure alignment on project goals, commitments, and timelines.

Skills & Experience:

  • 10+ years of experience in commercial software development.
  • Demonstrated excellence in working with cross functional teams in fast-paced environments, both in terms of technical leadership and cross team collaboration.
  • Excellent command of tools and expertise for troubleshooting production issues.
  • Experience around building scalable and distributed software systems, from conception to production.
  • Experience of software architecture, design principles and engineering best practices.

  • Employee assistance program. We’re here for you with resources and programs to help you through life’s challenges.

title: Senior Product Manager - Search & Ranking
description:
At Catawiki, every day brings the extraordinary! Whether it’s Daniel Ricciardo’s Formula 1 Car, a Woolly Mammoth’s Skeleton, Lady Gaga's Jumpsuit or Usain Bolt’s running shoe, we encounter exceptional objects every day.

We’re a one-of-a-kind marketplace for buying and selling special objects. Each week, more than 100,000 unique items are auctioned, all carefully curated by our passionate in-house experts.

Having sold over 25 million unique objects, our mission is to become the world’s most popular destination for special objects. As a growing, diverse and sustainable scale-up, we proudly live by three core values. If these values resonate with you, we’d love to explore how you can join us.

  • Taking ownership and driving impact 
  • Being open to change and feedback
  • Being passionate about our mission and our customers. 

Your mission

Every Product Manager at Catawiki owns a meaningful part of the customer experience.

In Search and Ranking, your mission is to help buyers find the special objects they care about. You will shape how search, ranking and personalisation work across the buyer journey, making discovery more relevant and helping more buyers find objects they love.

This is a broad product area. It brings together buyer needs, expert curation, marketplace priorities, search experiences and machine learning. You will identify the most important opportunities, set a clear direction and lead a cross functional team from insight to measurable customer and business impact.

The solution is not prescribed. You may improve search relevance, ranking, recommendations or personalisation, or explore new AI enabled ways to help buyers discover objects. What matters is that you solve a meaningful customer problem, measure the impact and scale what works.

You will own the strategy, outcomes and execution for this area, working closely with Engineering, Design, Data Science, Marketing and Commercial teams.

What you will do

  1. Set and communicate a clear product vision, strategy and roadmap for Search and Ranking.
  2. Own measurable outcomes across search relevance, discovery, engagement and buyer conversion.
  3. Use behavioural data, customer research and commercial insight to identify and prioritise the biggest opportunities.
  4. Turn ambiguous customer and business problems into clear hypotheses, prototypes and executable plans.
  5. Lead initiatives from early discovery through experimentation, launch and scaling.
  6. Define success metrics and build a rigorous experimentation agenda for search, ranking and personalisation.
  7. Work with machine learning engineers and data scientists to assess model quality, test new approaches and improve customer outcomes.
  8. Improve the relevance of search results and recommendations across the buyer journey.
  9. Integrate personalisation into the customer experience in ways that feel useful, coherent and trustworthy.
  10. Design, run and evaluate experiments, using positive, negative and inconclusive results to guide decisions.
  11. Use AI and rapid prototyping to test ideas early, reduce development risk and accelerate learning.
  12. Create clarity, momentum and accountability across teams, including when priorities or incentives differ.
  13. Communicate strategy, performance, tradeoffs and recommendations clearly to senior and C level stakeholders.

Who you are

Three qualities matter most in this role.

Outcome ownership

You take responsibility for customer and business results, not only for delivering features. You stay with the problem, remove obstacles and change direction when the evidence calls for it.

Systems thinking

You understand how search, ranking, recommendations, auction dynamics, expert curation and marketplace health influence one another. You make thoughtful decisions across the full buyer journey.

Experimental rigour

You use data, research, prototypes and controlled experiments to make decisions. You learn from negative results and can distinguish meaningful progress from activity.

You will also bring:

  1. At least five years of product management experience, preferably in consumer ecommerce, marketplaces or another digital product at scale.
  2. Experience owning a broad product area or customer journey, rather than only individual features.
  3. Experience defining product strategy or roadmaps for search, ranking, recommendations, personalisation or other machine learning products.
  4. Confidence working with product metrics, experiments and commercial performance.
  5. Experience designing, running and analysing A/B tests, including tests involving machine learning products.
  6. The ability to turn uncertain opportunities into clear hypotheses, prototypes and plans.
  7. A practical understanding of machine learning concepts and how models become useful product experiences.
  8. Experience working closely with machine learning engineers and data scientists to develop and improve customer facing features.
  9. Comfort using AI tools to prototype quickly and explore customer experiences.
  10. The ability to balance immediate commercial opportunities with longer term product and platform investments.
  11. Clear communication skills and the ability to influence senior leaders without relying on formal authority.
  12. The pace, resilience and judgement to maintain a high standard of execution in an ambiguous environment.

Where you will be

This role is based in Amsterdam. We offer a relocation package for people currently living outside the Netherlands.

Why You'll Love Working with Us

  • Create a visible impact by working at scale in a global organisation serving millions of customers across 80+ categories. In our flat structure, every role has a broad scope and directly impacts both our customers and the business.
  • Learn and grow through our Learning & Development initiatives, including clear development plans and mentorship programmes to support your career progression.
  • A culture of connection defines us. We’re a passionate, diverse team of 800+ Catawikians representing 60+ nationalities. We foster an inclusive and queer-friendly environment where everyone is encouraged to bring their full self to work.
  • Celebrate life’s moments with us. You’ll receive a €100 Catavoucher when you join, a €50 Catavoucher on your birthday, and an extra day off each year to “Pursue Your Passion”. We also offer additional leave for key work anniversaries and important life events. Benefits may vary by location.

Our Offices and Way of Working

Our vibrant offices in Amsterdam and Lisbon are designed to inspire collaboration. Most Catawikians operate in a hybrid setup, combining office-based and remote work, with a minimum of two days per week in the office, unless a role is explicitly stated as fully remote or fully office-based.

Interested?

Apply with an English CV and Cover Letter. By applying, you agree to Catawiki’s Applicant Privacy Policy. If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every requirement, we still encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support the review of your application. AI may help us assess how your experience matches the requirements of the role, but hiring decisions are always made by our recruitment team

title: Fullstack Web Developer
description:
Overview

We are looking for a hands-on Fullstack Web Developer to join our Web Apps team, in our Zürich office. In this role you will have the opportunity to drive development of new features, have a say in architecture and design decisions and have real impact across all the team’s projects.

The web apps team plays a central role at Auterion and owns the systems that add connectivity and remote interfaces for fleet management and operations. Our services are responsible for ingesting and analyzing flight telemetry data, managing and updating the fleet as well as integrating with other systems across the stack. 

The ideal candidate is someone who’s a self-starter, can work independently, can work with ambiguity, can take decisions on their own and not be afraid to drive and push towards getting the project across the finish line.

Responsibilities and Duties

  • Take ownership and drive the development of new features across all the team’s web based projects
  • Deliver clean, readable and maintainable code
  • Integrate services between edge devices and our centralized services
  • Handle new feature discovery, prototyping and investigations
  • Assist the Customer Success team in debugging and resolving customer issues
  • Monitor and analyze user usage patterns and other statistics
  • Push initiatives to clean up, upgrade, and refactor existing services to reduce technical debt
  • Maintain and improve integrations with 3rd party services

Qualifications and Skills

  • 4+ years of experience in a Fullstack web development or similar role.
  • Strong proficiency with the Node.js  ecosystem, development and tooling
  • Strong proficiency with the Typescript ecosystem, development and tooling

  • Solid experience with CI/CD pipelines (GoCD and GH Actions)
  • Experience with monitoring and observability tools (Datadog, Grafana)
  • Python proficiency is a plus
  • CH/EU citizenship required 

Benefits

  • Flexible working hours
  • Stock Options
  • Generous holiday allowance
  • Company pension plan 
  • Car parking  
  • Enhanced maternity & paternity leave
  • Mental health and wellbeing support

We are building the leading software platform for AI-powered autonomous systems for enterprise and government customers. Our team is supporting the most important missions and solving the most challenging problems.

At Auterion, we bring together the sharpest minds who love to solve the hardest problems. Join a vibrant team built on innovation, openness, and excellence, where you’ll be empowered to develop ideas, collaborate across all levels, and make an impact that matters.

raw.description:
About EH Group Engineering

EHG is developing cutting-edge fuel cell technology for heavy duty mobility and large-scale stationary power applications. Our uniquely redesigned product is a significantly more compact fuel cell with high power density and lower costs of production. Faced with the challenges of climate change and the transition to a decentralised energy system, EHG seeks to provide high performance and cost-effective fuel cell solutions to our clients and partners.

To help bring this vision to life, we are looking for a Senior Control Engineer to coordinate our efforts in designing control strategies for containerized systems integrating our fuel cell technology alongside equipment such as gas reformers, batteries, and climate control units. You will coordinate the control team and play a key role in shaping how these complex, multi-equipment systems operate safely and efficiently in the field.

Based in the US? You’re welcome to apply. This is an on-site role in Nyon, Switzerland. We ask that you relocate within 3 months of starting, and we’ll support you with a relocation package.

 

Key Responsibilities:

  • Coordinate the control engineering activities and define the control architecture and technical roadmap for our fuel cell and containerized power systems

  • Develop control strategies, models and algorithms for test-benches, fuel cell system and containerized power supply systems using Matlab/Simulink and Siemens PLCs

  • Coordinate the transition of prototype control algorithms from Simulink to industrial-quality code in TIA Portal Step 7

  • Implement, tune and validate controllers for thermal, air, fuel and power subsystems

  • Define and own control requirements, state machines and safety/diagnostic logic

  • Drive the continuous improvement (performance, efficiency and robustness) of our products

  • Define and oversee model-in-the-loop (MIL) testing and validation procedures

  • Manage the complete software life cycle, from requirements through release and maintenance, including dataset management

  • Establish coding standards, conduct code reviews and ensure compliance with industrial and certification requirements

  • Coordinate and develop the control team, including task planning and prioritization

  • Act as the main control interface with embedded, test and electrical engineering, as well as external partners and suppliers

 

Skills and Experience Required:

  • BSc/MSc in control, electrical, mechatronic or automation engineering is mandatory

  • Minimum 7 years of experience in control engineering, including at least 2 years in a technical lead or senior role

  • Skill 1 : Strong experience in process control engineering, particularly with containerized power supply systems; knowledge of programming and implementing safety PLCs is a strong plus

  • Skill 2 : Strong experience with TIA Portal (Step 7, WinCC, Test Suite), with the ability to structure code to industrial standards and meet certification requirements

  • Experience with functional safety (e.g. IEC 61508, ISO 13849), including SIL/PL determination and implementation of safety functions

  • Experience across the complete V-model development cycle, including hazard and risk assessment, requirements definition, safety requirements specification (SRS), verification and validation, and dataset management

  • Experience with stationary and maritime power applications, with a focus on the US and EU markets and their respective standards and certification requirements

  • Proven team player, with the ability to:
    (i) Coordinate and mentor the control team by clearly explaining your code and helping the team adopt robust industrial methods: you will take the responsibility in developing Skill 1 and Skill 2 across the team
    (ii) Collaborate effectively within interdisciplinary teams

  • Solid knowledge of control theory, state machines and system identification

  • Strong experience with MATLAB/Simulink and model-based design is a plus

  • Professional working language is in English.

     

Start date: Immediately

Faced with the challenges of climate change and the transition to a decentralised energy system, EHG seeks to provide high performance and cost-effective fuel cell solutions to our clients and partners.

To help bring this vision to life, we are looking for a Senior Control Engineer to coordinate our efforts in designing control strategies for containerized systems integrating our fuel cell technology alongside equipment such as gas reformers, batteries, and climate control units. You will coordinate the control team and play a key role in shaping how these complex, multi-equipment systems operate safely and efficiently in the field.

Based in the US? You’re welcome to apply. This is an on-site role in Nyon, Switzerland. We ask that you relocate within 3 months of starting, and we’ll support you with a relocation package.

 

Key Responsibilities:

  • Coordinate the control engineering activities and define the control architecture and technical roadmap for our fuel cell and containerized power systems

  • Develop control strategies, models and algorithms for test-benches, fuel cell system and containerized power supply systems using Matlab/Simulink and Siemens PLCs

  • Coordinate the transition of prototype control algorithms from Simulink to industrial-quality code in TIA Portal Step 7

  • Implement, tune and validate controllers for thermal, air, fuel and power subsystems

  • Define and own control requirements, state machines and safety/diagnostic logic

  • Drive the continuous improvement (performance, efficiency and robustness) of our products

  • Define and oversee model-in-the-loop (MIL) testing and validation procedures

  • Manage the complete software life cycle, from requirements through release and maintenance, including dataset management

  • Establish coding standards, conduct code reviews and ensure compliance with industrial and certification requirements

  • Coordinate and develop the control team, including task planning and prioritization

  • Act as the main control interface with embedded, test and electrical engineering, as well as external partners and suppliers

 

Skills and Experience Required:

  • BSc/MSc in control, electrical, mechatronic or automation engineering is mandatory

  • Minimum 7 years of experience in control engineering, including at least 2 years in a technical lead or senior role

  • Skill 1 : Strong experience in process control engineering, particularly with containerized power supply systems; knowledge of programming and implementing safety PLCs is a strong plus

  • Skill 2 : Strong experience with TIA Portal (Step 7, WinCC, Test Suite), with the ability to structure code to industrial standards and meet certification requirements

  • Experience with functional safety (e.g. IEC 61508, ISO 13849), including SIL/PL determination and implementation of safety functions

  • Experience across the complete V-model development cycle, including hazard and risk assessment, requirements definition, safety requirements specification (SRS), verification and validation, and dataset management

    (i) Coordinate and mentor the control team by clearly explaining your code and helping the team adopt robust industrial methods: you will take the responsibility in developing Skill 1 and Skill 2 across the team
    (ii) Collaborate effectively within interdisciplinary teams

  • Strong experience with MATLAB/Simulink and model-based design is a plus

  • Professional working language is in English.

     

Start date: Immediately

Founded in Switzerland, EHG is now expanding into the United States, fueled by exponential AI data center power demand and a soon-to-be-announced major investment round. This is a defining, high-growth chapter for the company.

 

The opportunity

We're hiring a Quality Manager to own a single quality system across both of our production streams — our established MW-scale facility in Nyon, Switzerland and our new US operation in Houston, Texas.

You'd be based in Nyon, where our production and process knowledge sits today, and own quality for the US operation as it stands up. The requirement is explicit: quality must be identical at both sites. Same specifications, same control plans, same acceptance criteria, same records. A customer taking delivery of a system should not be able to tell which site built the stack inside it, and our certification and warranty position depends on being able to demonstrate that.

Our customers are data center operators, defense programs, and industrial sites where reliability is the product. In your first year you'd harmonize our quality management system across both entities, establish controls in Houston that match those proven in Nyon as manufacturing technology transfers, build supplier quality alongside Supply Chain for a shared global supply base, and support certification of our systems for both European and US markets.

Location & travel: Nyon-based. Regular travel to Houston is expected as the US operation stands up, along with travel to supplier and partner sites in Europe and the US.

 

What you'll own

  • One quality management system across both entities — a common QMS covering Nyon and Houston, including the path to ISO 9001 certification in the US and alignment with what is already established in Switzerland.

  • Equivalence between sites. A single set of product specifications, control plans, inspection criteria, and acceptance standards, with a defined process for how any change is applied at both sites rather than one.

  • In-process quality for fuel cell stack production at both locations, including the process controls that matter most in stack assembly — cleanliness and contamination control, leak testing, torque and compression control, and alignment.

  • Supplier quality for a shared global supply base, working with Supply Chain on qualification, audits, first article inspection, part submission, and ongoing performance, with one qualification standard regardless of which site a supplier serves.

  • Quality oversight of contract manufacturing and assembly partners building balance of plant and containerized systems on our behalf in both regions — audits, quality agreements, source inspection, and acceptance criteria.

  • Nonconformance and corrective action across both sites, including NCR and CAPA processes and structured problem solving, with findings at one site systematically applied at the other.

  • Traceability and product records — a common lot genealogy model from raw material through stack serial to delivered system, and the test and inspection data that supports warranty, certification, and customer acceptance, held consistently across both entities.

  • Certification across regions, working with external certification partners on the standards applicable to stationary hydrogen power systems in Europe and the US, authority having jurisdiction approvals, and marine classification where relevant.

  • Quality culture on both floors, including operator training, work instruction discipline, and establishing the habits in Houston that are already proven in Nyon, as US headcount grows quickly.

  • Building the US quality capability, defining what needs to sit on the ground in Houston versus what is run centrally from Nyon, and recruiting into it as volumes grow.

 

What we're looking for

Core experience

  • Owning quality across more than one manufacturing site, ideally in more than one country, with a demonstrated ability to hold two sites to genuinely the same standard from a distance.

  • Establishing or substantially rebuilding a quality function, including authoring a quality management system rather than administering an existing one.

  • Hands-on in-process and incoming quality in a production setting, with real familiarity with control plans, inspection methods, measurement systems, and process capability.

  • Supplier quality experience, including auditing suppliers and holding them to standard.

  • Structured problem solving and root cause analysis, with a track record of permanently closing out recurring defects.

  • Working knowledge of product certification processes and the evidence they require, ideally in energy, power equipment, or another regulated product category. Exposure to both European and US regimes is a strong advantage.

  • The judgment to know which controls are essential at low volume and which can wait, and the confidence to hold a quality position under schedule pressure.

  • Comfort working across time zones and influencing a site you are not physically based at, including building quality capability remotely.

Especially compelling

  • Fuel cell, battery cell, or similar electrochemical assembly experience.

  • Experience with cleanliness-critical or contamination-sensitive assembly processes.

  • Experience supporting a technology transfer between sites or countries, and establishing quality at the receiving end.

  • Experience qualifying and auditing contract manufacturers or system integrators.

  • Startup or scale-up experience as an early hire during hyper-growth.

  • Experience working between Europe and the US, and with US codes and certification practice in particular. French is useful but not required.

 

What we offer

  • Competitive compensation and meaningful equity, calibrated to the market and discussed directly with you.

  • Relocation support to Nyon, Switzerland.

  • The opportunity to build EHG's global quality function during a defining phase of hyper-growth.

Note: Swiss work authorization or eligibility is required for this role, along with the ability to travel to the United States.

 

EH Group is an equal opportunity employer. We value a diverse workforce and an inclusive culture, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

  • In-process quality for fuel cell stack production at both locations, including the process controls that matter most in stack assembly — cleanliness and contamination control, leak testing, torque and compression control, and alignment.

  • Supplier quality for a shared global supply base, working with Supply Chain on qualification, audits, first article inspection, part submission, and ongoing performance, with one qualification standard regardless of which site a supplier serves.

  • Quality oversight of contract manufacturing and assembly partners building balance of plant and containerized systems on our behalf in both regions — audits, quality agreements, source inspection, and acceptance criteria.

  • Nonconformance and corrective action across both sites, including NCR and CAPA processes and structured problem solving, with findings at one site systematically applied at the other.

  • Traceability and product records — a common lot genealogy model from raw material through stack serial to delivered system, and the test and inspection data that supports warranty, certification, and customer acceptance, held consistently across both entities.

  • Certification across regions, working with external certification partners on the standards applicable to stationary hydrogen power systems in Europe and the US, authority having jurisdiction approvals, and marine classification where relevant.

  • Quality culture on both floors, including operator training, work instruction discipline, and establishing the habits in Houston that are already proven in Nyon, as US headcount grows quickly.

  • Building the US quality capability, defining what needs to sit on the ground in Houston versus what is run centrally from Nyon, and recruiting into it as volumes grow.

 

What we're looking for

Core experience

  • Owning quality across more than one manufacturing site, ideally in more than one country, with a demonstrated ability to hold two sites to genuinely the same standard from a distance.

  • Establishing or substantially rebuilding a quality function, including authoring a quality management system rather than administering an existing one.

  • Hands-on in-process and incoming quality in a production setting, with real familiarity with control plans, inspection methods, measurement systems, and process capability.

  • Supplier quality experience, including auditing suppliers and holding them to standard.

  • Structured problem solving and root cause analysis, with a track record of permanently closing out recurring defects.

  • Working knowledge of product certification processes and the evidence they require, ideally in energy, power equipment, or another regulated product category. Exposure to both European and US regimes is a strong advantage.

  • The judgment to know which controls are essential at low volume and which can wait, and the confidence to hold a quality position under schedule pressure.

  • Comfort working across time zones and influencing a site you are not physically based at, including building quality capability remotely.

Especially compelling

  • Fuel cell, battery cell, or similar electrochemical assembly experience.

  • Experience with cleanliness-critical or contamination-sensitive assembly processes.

  • Experience supporting a technology transfer between sites or countries, and establishing quality at the receiving end.

  • Experience qualifying and auditing contract manufacturers or system integrators.

  • Startup or scale-up experience as an early hire during hyper-growth.

  • Experience working between Europe and the US, and with US codes and certification practice in particular. French is useful but not required.

 

What we offer

  • Competitive compensation and meaningful equity, calibrated to the market and discussed directly with you.

  • Relocation support to Nyon, Switzerland.

  • The opportunity to build EHG's global quality function during a defining phase of hyper-growth.

Note: Swiss work authorization or eligibility is required for this role, along with the ability to travel to the United States.

title: Manager Operations Planning & Performance
description: Bij Crisp hebben we een missie: eten met meer smaak bereikbaar maken voor iedereen. Daarvoor moet elke schakel in onze operatie, van warehouse tot voordeur, dagelijks naadloos op elkaar aansluiten. Als Manager Operations Planning & Performance ben jij de spil tussen wat de klant bestelt en hoe wij dat logistiek waarmaken. Je brengt alle operationele schakels samen in één strakke, integrale planning en bouwt mee aan een betrouwbare operatie die klaar is om slim door te groeien. Wat je gaat doen Je bent eigenaar van de integrale operationele planning. Je vertaalt verwachte klantvraag naar concrete capaciteit op de weg (hoeveel bezorgers hebben we per dag en per hub nodig?) en bepaalt samen met de Operations Manager de planningsstrategie voor de korte en middellange termijn. Je zorgt voor een strakke planning tussen Delivery, Retentie en Warehouse. Zo werkt iedereen vanuit dezelfde basis en tilt jouw scherpe blik onze processen naar een hoger niveau. Je geeft leiding aan een team van routeplanners (werkstudenten en starters). Samen zorgen jullie dagelijks voor de meest efficiënte bezorgroutes. Jouw team staat in direct contact met de bezorghubs, het warehouse en de growth afdeling om de capaciteit af te stemmen Je werkt nauw samen met teams door de hele organisatie, van Tech en Analytics tot Recruitment. Om te weten wat er speelt, ben je regelmatig te vinden waar het gebeurt: op onze bezorghubs en in het warehouse. Je stuurt op operationele KPI’s (zoals Drops per Hour en Time per Stop ) en beheert belangrijke kostenlijnen. Samen met de Regiomanager en Business Analyst Delivery blijf je ons bezorgnetwerk continu optimaliseren. Je bent eindverantwoordelijk voor de lijn tussen ons warehouse en de hubs. Je onderhoudt de contacten met vrachtwagenvervoerders, stuurt op prestaties ( On Time ) en kosten ( Cost per Drop ) en maximaliseert de vulgraad. Je kijkt altijd naar wat beter kan, houdt trends en innovaties in de markt in de gaten en draagt dit actief aan wanneer je hier kansen ziet. Je signaleert kansen in de operatie, maakt de impact inzichtelijk en leidt verbeterprojecten van idee tot implementatie, bijvoorbeeld op het gebied van servicetijd, automatisering van planningstaken of de inrichting van ons netwerk. Je bent onderdeel van het Delivery team en rapporteert aan de Head of Delivery. Dit ben jij Je hebt HBO/WO werk- en denkniveau en minimaal 3 jaar werkervaring in operationele planning, logistiek of supply chain, bij voorkeur in een snelgroeiende e-commerce- of retailomgeving. Je beweegt je makkelijk door de hele organisatie, van de vloer tot het management. Je zoekt actief de samenwerking op en krijgt verschillende teams moeiteloos op één lijn. Je creëert draagvlak en krijgt mensen mee in een gezamenlijke aanpak, ook als je geen formele zeggenschap over ze hebt Je bent sterk met data. Je duikt zelf in de cijfers, bouwt een model of dashboard als dat nodig is, en vertaalt analyses naar concrete keuzes voor de operatie. Ervaring met SQL, BigQuery en Data Studio is een pré. Jij kijkt verder dan je eigen scope en overziet de hele keten. Je begrijpt hoe een keuze in de planning doorwerkt in het warehouse, op de weg en bij de klant, en je weet de juiste balans te vinden tussen kosten en kwaliteit. Je bent resultaatgericht en weet wat het is om eigenaarschap te nemen. Jij maakt dingen graag makkelijk en concreet. Complexe vraagstukken zet jij gemakkelijk om naar begrijpelijke acties. Je houdt het hoofd koel als het even spannend wordt. Pieken, onverwachte uitval of last-minute wijzigingen brengen je niet van je stuk; je prioriteert, plant opnieuw en zorgt dat de operatie doordraait. Je spreekt vloeiend Nederlands en Engels. Wat wij bieden Werken bij een B Corp gecertificeerd bedrijf, waarbij je de kans krijgt om je stempel te drukken op het Europese voedselsysteem. 27 vakantiedagen om bij te komen en op te laden. Een extra vrije dag per jaar om je in te zetten voor vrijwilligerswerk en iets goeds te doen. Aandacht voor je mentale gezondheid met online begeleiding van erkende psychologen via OpenUp. Voor straks een perfect pensioen via BPFL. Elke maand food for thought, met workshops en talks via de Crisp University. Regelmatig tastings of workshops op kantoor of bij een van onze leveranciers, om te zien hoe onze lekkerste producten worden gemaakt – en natuurlijk ook te proeven. Dagelijks een uitgebreide, georganiseerde lunch op kantoor. Enthousiaste, slimme collega’s en tijd om elkaar te leren kennen tijdens sport, events en proeverijen. En... fikse korting op je Crisp boodschappen, omdat je thuis natuurlijk ook goed wilt eten. Onze selectieprocedure Solliciteer via onderstaande button. Hoe meer je kunt delen over jezelf en de reden dat je solliciteert, hoe beter. Bij Crisp streven we naar een inclusieve en diverse werkomgeving waarin iedereen welkom is, ongeacht hun achtergrond, geslacht, leeftijd, etniciteit, seksuele geaardheid, religie of beperking. Wij moedigen sollicitanten met diverse perspectieven en achtergronden aan om te solliciteren en geloven in gelijke kansen voor iedereen. We waarderen de unieke bijdragen die elke medewerker kan leveren en zijn vastbesloten om een inclusieve werkplek te creëren waarin iedereen wordt gerespecteerd en gewaardeerd. title: Project Leider Bouw
description: Monumental automatiseert de bouw met robotica en software. Onze missie is om de bouw software-defined en autonoom te maken – een toekomst waarin mooie gebouwen op maat in één dag verrijzen, met minimale inzet van handwerk. We zijn een groeiend team van engineers, operators en technici, afkomstig van bedrijven als Palantir, Qualcomm, Dyson, Shopify, Tesla, Meta en Google DeepMind. We staan nog aan het begin van het opbouwen van dit bedrijf, en dit is je kans om buitenproportioneel veel impact te maken op een probleem dat écht uitmaakt. Vanaf dag één werk je samen met een ervaren foundingteam, met een Series B van $32M achter ons onder leiding van Khosla Ventures en Plural. Monumental zit in het centrum van Amsterdam, in een prachtig pand met een volledig uitgeruste werkplaats en een eigen testvloer voor robots. We bouwen de hele stack in-house – hardware én software. We zijn uitdrukkelijk geen hybride of remote-first bedrijf: robots en muren bouw je niet vanaf je keukentafel, dus we werken vijf dagen per week op locatie. Lees meer over waarom wij vinden dat je je tijd aan de bouw zou moeten besteden, en over onze visie en ons bedrijf . Misschien vind je ons YouTube-kanaal interessant, de film van Based in Europe over hoe we het Europese woningtekort aanpakken , of deze video van Andreas Klinger over hoe ons kantoor eruitziet. Over de functie De afgelopen jaren is Monumental gegroeid van een werkend product en de eerste proefprojecten naar bouwen op grote schaal. Inmiddels hebben we een vloot van meer dan 150 robots, die metselwerk hebben uitgevoerd voor meer dan 90 woningen, een school, een buurthuis, een hotel en meer dan 150 meter kanaalwand. Elke maand nemen we meer bouwprojecten aan, intern noemen we die ‘deployments’. We werken met meer robots en meer mensen en breiden vanuit Nederland uit naar het Verenigd Koninkrijk en de VS. Als Hub Lead zet je onze eerste vestiging buiten het hoofdkantoor op, in het noorden van Nederland. Je begint met ons grootste bouwproject tot nu toe. Naarmate er meer projecten bijkomen, bouw je het team en de operatie verder uit. We zoeken mensen die breed inzetbaar zijn en een bouwproject willen leiden alsof het hun eigen bedrijf is. Achter elk project staat een Deployment Manager die van begin tot eind verantwoordelijk is. In de praktijk vervul je vijf rollen tegelijk: uitvoerder, operationeel manager, accountmanager, analist en projectmanager. Je maakt het bouwplan, voert het met je team als onderaannemer uit, onderhoudt het contact met de aannemer en zorgt dat we goed metselwerk op tijd opleveren. Dat doe je in de bouw, waar plannen voortdurend veranderen. Uiteindelijk leid je meerdere projecten tegelijk, waaronder complexe projecten waarbij veel op het spel staat. De ene dag sta je bij zonsopgang op en ga je naar de bouwplaats. Je zaagt stenen, bewaakt de planning, stemt af met de hoofdaannemer en ziet je bouwplan steen voor steen werkelijkheid worden. De rol past goed bij je als je eerder een bedrijf hebt opgericht, of als je een ondernemende functie zoekt waarin je veel invloed hebt op het resultaat. Wat je gaat doen De logistiek van een bouwproject plannen. Je bepaalt hoeveel en welke robots en mensen nodig zijn, stemt af met andere onderaannemers en maakt de dagelijkse planning. Tegelijk houd je het grotere geheel in het oog en begrijp je wat jouw keuzes betekenen voor de kosten en opbrengsten per project. Op de bouwplaats het team aansturen, begeleiden en motiveren. Je onderhoudt het contact met hoofdaannemers en andere betrokkenen, vertegenwoordigt Monumental en legt uit wat we doen. Je schakelt net zo makkelijk met steigerbouwers als met de CEO’s van de grootste hoofdaannemers en onze engineers. Operationele systemen opzetten waarmee elk project beter verloopt dan het vorige. Je ziet waar tijd en middelen verloren gaan, past processen aan en verbetert de marge. Samenwerken met bestaande klanten en zorgen dat daar nieuwe bouwprojecten uit voortkomen. In de toekomst doe je dat ook voor aanverwante productlijnen buiten het metselwerk. Verantwoordelijkheid nemen voor de winst- en verliesrekening van je project en voorstellen doen om de kosten en opbrengsten per project steeds verder te verbeteren. Helpen bij het werven en interviewen van nieuwe robotoperators en deployment operators. Wat we zoeken Minimaal drie jaar ervaring startupervaring, als operator, manager, of founder. Nederlands als moedertaal. De bouwsector is sterk lokaal georganiseerd, dus dit is een vereiste voor de functie. Je communiceert helder en makkelijk met mensen met uiteenlopende achtergronden. Je bent bereid om letterlijk je handen vuil te maken om het werk gedaan te krijgen. Je komt snel in actie, zet door en krijgt dingen voor elkaar. In deze functie draait het vooral om uitvoeren. Je kunt goed omgaan met hoge werkdruk. Op bouwplaatsen gaat regelmatig iets mis en staat er veel op het spel. Daar komt bij dat we nieuwe technologie inzetten waarvan we nog niet alle mogelijke storingen kennen. Je denkt scherp en leert graag. Welke achtergrond je ook hebt, je zult in deze rol veel en snel moeten leren. Het werk kan elke drie tot zes maanden als een nieuwe baan voelen. Je leert veel over de bouw, robotica en werken in een snelgroeiend technologiebedrijf. Je hebt ervaring met het aansturen van een klein team en weet hoe je mensen begeleidt en motiveert. Je bent operationeel en analytisch sterk. Je kunt een helder operationeel plan uitwerken in een spreadsheet, een winst- en verliesrekening presenteren en verschillende scenario’s doorrekenen, inclusief de factoren die het resultaat bepalen. Je bent een sterke projectmanager. Waarom Monumental? Bij Monumental werken betekent vooroplopen in een beweging die de bouwsector wezenlijk wil veranderen. Jouw werk heeft hier niet alleen impact op het bedrijf, maar op de toekomst van hoe we bouwen. Als je gedreven wordt door innovatie, graag complexe uitdagingen aanpakt en klaar bent om echt verschil te maken, horen we graag van je. Voor open sollicitaties (als je geen rol ziet die precies past) kun je ons mailen op: Helaas bieden we op dit moment geen stageplekken aan. Voldoe je niet aan alle eisen hierboven, maar ben je enthousiast over Monumental en denk je dat je ons toch kunt helpen moeilijke problemen op te lossen? Neem dan contact op. We verwelkomen generalisten die op resultaat gericht zijn en graag on the job leren. Find more English Speaking Jobs in Netherlands on Arbeitnow

title: Director, Expanded Access Program Operations
description: About myTomorrows myTomorrows is a global health tech company dedicated to breaking down barriers for patients seeking treatment options. We strive to enable earlier and better treatment access by bridging the gap between those searching for possible options, and the companies who develop them. We work closely with patients, healthcare professionals, trial sites, patient advocacy groups, and BioPharma – connecting key stakeholders in the drug development ecosystem. We’ve developed a cutting-edge AI-powered technology platform that simplifies and streamlines access to drugs in development. To support our users and clients, we have a range of industry-expert specialized teams ready to help. Our services include clinical trial patient recruitment, Expanded Access Program management and Real-World Data collection. With a global footprint spanning 134 countries, to date we’ve supported over 17,000 patients, 3,000 physicians and 350 sites, earning the trust of 60+ BioPharma companies. In October 2025, we closed a €25M investment with Avego Healthcare Capital to fuel our global ambitions and scale the business. Join us in shaping the future of treatment access - making tomorrow’s therapies accessible for people who need them today. The opportunity: Director of EAP Operations (Expanded Access Programs and Site Management) This is a high‑impact leadership role at the heart of how myTomorrows delivers Expanded Access Programs (EAPs) globally—where operational excellence meets commercial acumen. As Director of EAP Operations, you’ll own the end‑to‑end operational delivery of our EAP portfolio, integrating Program Management and Site Management into one scalable, outcome‑driven model. Beyond ensuring quality, compliance, speed, and resilience, you’ll be expected to think like an entrepreneur: spotting opportunities, optimising processes, and driving commercially sound decisions that enable sustainable growth. You’ll be a core member of the Operations Leadership Team and report directly to our COO (Vanessa says hi). This role is perfect for someone who thrives on complexity, builds high‑performing teams, and raises the operational bar—while balancing patient‑first decision‑making with a strong commercial mindset. Geographic Requirement: This role is open to candidates in The Netherlands, United Kingdom, Canada and USA. For candidates in North America , to ensure seamless collaboration with our teams, applicants must reside within the EST or CST time zones . What you'll do in this role: Own the end-to-end operating model for EAP Program + Site Management, ensuring scalable and compliant delivery Translate strategy and portfolio forecasts into capacity planning, org design and hiring priorities Build resilient coverage and escalation models across the portfolio (no single points of failure) Lead the EAP Program Management team to deliver consistent execution across clients and geographies Lead the EAP Site Management team to ensure strong site engagement, workload balance and service performance Drive standardisation and continuous improvement across ways of working, tooling and operational excellence Set and run a strong governance rhythm: KPIs, performance reviews, risk management and quality oversight Act as senior escalation point for complex delivery, regulatory and stakeholder challenges Grow a bar-raising leadership bench through coaching, performance management and succession planning Partner with Finance, People and Operations on budgeting, workforce planning and scale-up decisions What you bring to the table: You have 8–10+ years experience leading and managing expanded access programs. Experience in a market access setting and with multi-country reimbursement strategies is a plus. You understand the EAP business, and have a strong and proven commercial and client service mindset. You have proven experience building and leading high performance teams. You know how to lead managers and scale operational teams in complex settings You have an exceptionally strong understanding of compliance, regulatory frameworks and operational requirements in the context of Expanded Access Programs You have a track record of operational excellence: scaling delivery, managing risk, and raising performance standards You are a strategic thinker with strong execution focus — you simplify complexity and drive outcomes You are a confident stakeholder manager who can align senior leaders and external partners You hold a high bar for quality and accountability, with calm leadership under pressure What success in the first 6 months looks like: Have full grip on the EAP portfolio and delivery realities — and you can clearly articulate the biggest operational opportunities and risks (and have recommendations on how to address them) Create clarity across Program & Site Management: ownership, workflows, escalation paths, and what “great” looks like Have strengthened the operating model to improve consistency, speed and resilience across the portfolio Have managed to deliver on the expected ramp-up of the EAP business both in terms of patients served, and revenue generated. Have implemented a clear KPI rhythm (quality, timelines, compliance, service levels) with transparent performance reporting Have improved capacity planning and coverage, educing single points of failure and enabling predictable delivery Have made at least 1–2 concrete operational improvements (process / tooling / standardisation) that measurably improve delivery outcomes Are seen as a trusted Operations Leadership Team member who raises the bar and builds momentum. DataSnipper is a $1B, bootstrapped unicorn with 600,000+ users across 180+ countries, already embedded in the daily workflows of top audit and accounting firms. Now, we are taking things further with our Excel Agent, bringing AI directly into where the work actually happens. Unlike generic AI tools, we do not sit on the sidelines. Our AI operates inside Excel, with access to real documents and audit evidence, meaning it does not just generate answers, it does the work, with full traceability. We are not just applying AI, we are redefining how audit gets done. If you want to build something category-defining at scale, this is the place. Translate DataSnipper's capabilities into language and use cases that resonate with audit professionals directly. Support Sales in building ROI cases that resonate with audit leadership. Surface patterns that require audit expertise to interpret - methodology gaps, adoption friction specific to audit processes, feedback that non-audit CSMs are less positioned to identify. Contribute Audit Knowledge to the Team: Help peers understand audit customer context. Act as an accessible internal resource for audit-specific questions to help raise the team's collective ability to serve audit accounts. Maintain Systems and Portfolio Data: Keep customer data, health signals, and portfolio records accurate and up to date in internal systems. Use this data to make better decisions and support reliable reporting. What You Bring Audit Domain Credibility: You have worked in or directly alongside audit teams. You understand engagement lifecycles, sample testing, evidence management, team hierarchies, and the quality standards that govern audit work. This is not background knowledge - it is something you apply directly in customer conversations and account planning. Concretely, you would be walking into billions of usage events flowing from our Excel Add-in, web apps and product backends through Azure Event Hubs into Snowflake; a dbt estate built on medallion principles and managed in dbt Cloud; Terraform-managed Snowflake and Azure infrastructure; and a set of product teams shipping AI agents faster than we can instrument them.

You will also find real, named open problems rather than a tidy platform: event capture mid-consolidation, multiple methods of user attribution, and a data quality layer that is designed but not yet built. We would rather tell you that up front.

Lead the team

  • Lead a team of two data engineers through outcomes, not tasks: set clear goals with the team and trust them to figure out how

  • Make the team measurably better: raise the engineering bar, grow each engineer into bigger problems, and address performance issues directly when they arise

  • Run regular 1:1s, give clear and timely feedback, and own each engineer's goals and development

  • Foster a culture of experimentation, learning, documentation and operational excellence

  • Partner closely with Product, Engineering, Customer Success and GTM to shape the team's roadmap, turning vague data requests into scoped, well-defined work

  • Make the trade-offs a small team serving the whole company needs: what to build, what to defer, and when a request shouldn't become a pipeline

  • Set the technical direction and make the architectural calls that shape the team's systems

  • Keep Snowflake performance and cost, tech debt, dependencies and compliance obligations (audit logging, vulnerability remediation, Vanta evidence) visible and under control

  • Be the person other engineering teams come to when they need to instrument something new

  • Contribute to the event ingestion architecture end to end: Azure Event Hubs, Snowpipe, Fivetran, and our shared Python/TypeScript event client libraries

  • Define and enforce event contracts and schemas so product teams can instrument new features without silent breakage downstream

  • Evolve the core data models (event, user, license, company) and integrate new sources such as product backends, MongoDB, HubSpot and billing

  • Guide reverse ETL and activation work that pushes modeled data back into HubSpot, MongoDB, Postgres and GTM reporting

Leadership

  • At least 1 year leading engineers as a team lead or engineering manager: 1:1s, feedback, goal setting, performance, and development
